references.text: Earlier, the carved images (פְּסִילִים) at Gilgal are mentioned, the same place where Ehud passes during his escape.
The context of Ehud's escape - his servants hesitated (הִתְמַהְמְהָם) to open the doors, giving Ehud time to flee.
Continuation of the story - after fleeing to Seira, Ehud reaches the hill country of Ephraim and blows a trumpet.
Lot is urged to flee to the mountains, a similar escape motif to seeking refuge.
Gilgal is mentioned in connection with the Israelites setting up the twelve stones there, near the place with the carved images.
